claim_1.claim: CyTOF analysis of PBMCs from 52 COVID-19 patients and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls across Hong Kong and Atlanta showed increased plasmablast and effector CD8 T cell frequencies in infected individuals, prolonged effector CD8 T cell kinetics up to day 40 after symptom onset, reduced plasmacytoid dendritic cell frequencies, reduced pS6 in pDCs, decreased IκBα in myeloid dendritic cells, and reduced HLA-DR on monocytes and mDCs in severe COVID-19 versus healthy controls.

sources.section: Analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes from COVID-19 patients by mass cytometry
sources.quote: We used mass cytometry to assess immune responses to SARS-CoV-2 infection in 52 COVID-19 patients, who were confirmed positive for viral RNA by polymerase chain reaction (PCR), and 62 age- and gender-matched healthy controls distributed between the two cohorts.

sources.section: Analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes from COVID-19 patients by mass cytometry
sources.quote: There was a notable increase in the frequency of plasmablast and effector CD8 T cells in all infected individuals ( Fig. 1B ) in both cohorts.

sources.section: Analysis of peripheral blood leukocytes from COVID-19 patients by mass cytometry
sources.quote: There were several differences, but notably the frequency of plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was significantly reduced in the PBMCs of SARS-CoV-2–infected individuals in both cohorts ( Fig. 1C ).

claim_2.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of ex vivo stimulated PBMCs from COVID-19 patients showed reduced production of IFN-α and TNF-α in plasmacytoid dendritic cells compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: COVID-19 results in functional impairment of blood myeloid cells and pDCs
sources.quote: Consistent with our hypothesis, there was reduced production of IFN-α in response to the TLR stimuli in the pDCs of infected individuals compared with those of healthy controls ( Fig. 2A ).

claim_3.claim: Olink analysis of plasma from COVID-19 patients showed significant up-regulation of 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: Enhanced concentrations of cytokines and inflammatory mediators in plasma from COVID-19 patients
sources.quote: Of the 92 analytes measured, 71 proteins were detected within the dynamic range of the assay. Of these 71 proteins, 43 cytokines, including IL-6, MCP-3, and CXCL10, were significantly up-regulated in COVID-19 infection ( Fig. 3 , top row, and fig. S6).

claim_4.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from COVID-19 patients revealed clusters of T cells and monocytes characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes such as IFI27, IFITM3, and ISG15, which were not present in healthy controls.

sources.section: Single-cell transcriptional response to COVID-19 infection
sources.quote: Notably, we detected clusters of T cells and monocytes that were characterized by the expression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) such as IFI27, IFITM3, or ISG15 (see C11-C MONO_IFN and C18-T_IFN in fig. S10). These IFN response–enriched clusters emerged only in samples from COVID-19 patients (fig. S12).

claim_5.claim: Q-PCR analysis of plasma from severe and ICU COVID-19 patients showed significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA compared to healthy controls.

sources.section: Severe COVID-19 infection is associated with the systemic release of bacterial products
sources.quote: Notably, the plasma of severe and ICU patients had significantly higher levels of bacterial DNA, as measured by PCR quantitation of bacterial 16 S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene product, and of LPS, as measured by a TLR4-based reporter assay ( Fig. 6, A and B ).
